## Worker stall detection (CCP local amendment, SP-034 - dies on pi-spine reinstall; durable copy in spine-tasks/SP-034-stall-detector-probe/record.md)

`lane.heartbeat worker_alive` watches PROCESS liveness only - a worker can sit at 0 CPU on a dead API call while heartbeats keep firing (k3 silent-wedge class, twice proven 2026-07-22: SP-027 run-1 84-min wedge; SP-029 replacement 25-min severe-latency crawl that SELF-RECOVERED). Before treating a long-silent lane as wedged, run the probe:

```powershell
pwsh Tools/spine-worker-probe.ps1 -BatchId <batchId> [-Lane N]   # 2 x 15s tree-CPU-delta windows + file-write delta over the lane worktrees
```

| Probe verdict | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `alive-progressing` | Writes during the probe, or tree CPU clearly active | Stand down; keep waiting |
| `alive-crawling` | Tree CPU above ~0 but in/near the observed 0.03-0.16s/15s crawl band, OR CPU-zero with a sub-30-min write drought | Severe provider latency - STAND DOWN (SP-029 self-recovered from exactly this); re-probe later |
| `wedged` | 0.00s tree CPU delta over BOTH windows AND newest-write age >= 30 min (incident-1 proven-dead rule) | T-10 candidate - see kill discipline below |

**Kill discipline:** the probe NEVER kills on its own; it prints the `Stop-Process` command for the wedged class only. The kill decision stays with steering judgment: (1) salvage the lane dirty WIP first (commit marked UNVERIFIED provenance), (2) duplicate-worker sweep - resume spawns a replacement WITHOUT reaping the original (wave recovery rule), (3) budget/stall context check. Only then run the printed T-10 command.
